text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: gpu-prefill OOM detected on prod-gpu-pool (us-west-2). Multiple containers restarted on node gpu-node-17, 12 restarts in 2m. Escalating to oncall.

carol: oncall here, looking. any customer impact reported?

alice: seeing elevated 5xxs from gateway, some streaming sessions drop. Not full outage but degraded for ~10% of requests to redwood-alpha-13b.

bob: grabbing runtime logs now. main error is CUDA OOM during prefill -> container receives SIGTERM and k8s restarts it. snippet:```
[2026-03-18T09:12:45Z] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (2.1 GiB requested)
[2026-03-18T09:12:45Z] runtime: prefill failed, aborting with SIGTERM
[2026-03-18T09:12:46Z] containerd: restarting container
```

dave: looks like long-context prefill (user sent ~180k tokens) + aggressive kv-prefetch. Prefetch brought model memory above threshold and triggered driver OOM.

carol: immediate mitigations we can do now?

bob: two quick ones: 1) route new requests for the model to fallback smaller variant (alpha-13b -> alpha-7b) via runtime fallback policy, 2) temporarily disable kv-prefetch and streaming prefetch on affected pool.

alice: I'll cordon the node and evict remaining pods to avoid noisy neighbor restarts. running:```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

alice: drain started, evictions in progress.

erin: compiling impacted customer list from logs, will paste shortly. initial hit shows 6 customers with elevated error rates, 2 enterprise customers with SLA alerts.

frank: heads-up to CustSuccess: preparing an email for the two enterprise customers, hold until we confirm scope.

bob: pushing a runtime config toggle to canary pool to disable kv-prefetch and set prefill token cap to 32k:```
# runtime-config: temporary emergency flags
prefetch.enabled=false
prefill.max_tokens=32000
```

dave: canary flip in 30s. monitoring memory usage on canary nodes.

bob: canary nodes show mem drop ~20%, no OOMs after flip. good sign. rolling to remaining nodes in affected pool with 1 node at a time.

alice: node cordon/evict completed. restarting empty node back into rotation after patch.

erin: customer list: acct-834, acct-901, acct-112, acct-773, acct-456, acct-999. acct-901 + acct-456 flagged for SLA. sending to frank.

frank: drafting message now, will include ETA for mitigation and note degraded requests.

carol: any telemetry evidence of a single huge prompt user or automated job?

bob: yes, trace id 0x7a2f shows a single session with multiple concatenated documents hitting 180k tokens. looks like a customer-side ingest script sent large batch.

dave: we should add a server-side hard cap for prefill windows + better circuit breaker to reject prefill requests above 64k tokens.

alice: creating incident ticket INC-2026-045 and will link to postmortem template.

alice: ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INC-2026-045

carol: timeline for hotfix and rollout?

bob: emergency hotfix: config toggle + prefill cap already rolling; full runtime patch to enforce stricter kv eviction and backpressure will be deployed in next 2 hours to all clusters.

dave: after patch, we'll enable per-customer prefill blocking for extremely long sessions and add telemetry alert for prefill > 50k tokens.

erin: support will open cases for the 6 impacted customers and attach request traces.

frank: sent initial customer note to the two SLA customers (internal copy only). will update when we confirm full mitigation.

carol: OK — mitigation in progress, grafting to oncall runbook. handoff: I'll leave this in a high state; night oncall get-rolled at 23:00UTC, pass to them with summary in incident channel.

alice: postmortem owner assigned to bob + dave. please capture root cause, why prefetch didn't cap, and recommended limits.

bob: capturing logs and will run a regression test against long-context workloads.

carol: thanks all. keep this thread for live updates only. after we close, move postmortem to #postmortems and link here. :white_check_mark:
